prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution delivers 1,000,000 village health pods with diagnostics and telehealth, so the Main KPI is not met by existing work. The largest deployed telehealth-at-the-village network is India's eSanjeevani hub-and-spoke service, linking about 142,000 Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes by September 2026 (https://newsonair.gov.in/esanjeevani-achieves-milestone-of-50-cr-teleconsultations-from-across-the-country/), but these are staffed health centres, not self-contained diagnostic pods, and they cover one country. Unstaffed booth programmes are small: Ping An's One-minute Clinics reported contracts for nearly 1,000 units in 2019 (https://newshubasia.com/opinion/ping-an-good-doctor-launches-commercial-operation-of-one-minute-clinics-and-signs-contracts-for-nearly-1000-units-serving-more-than-3-million-users), and kiosk pilots such as iKure report tens of units. Open source exists for the software layer (OpenMRS, Bahmni, Intelehealth tele-consult on OpenMRS: https://sites.google.com/a/intelehealth.io/team-wiki/the-intelehealth-platform), not for a replicable pod with diagnostics. Honest limit: the components (point-of-care tests, open EMR, teleconsultation) are well known; a task that only reassembles them needs its own prior-art basis.
